subsystems.name: Nutrient core
subsystems.role: holds the fertiliser payload in a concentrated, plant-available form.

subsystems.name: Stimuli-responsive shell
subsystems.role: encapsulates the core and breaks down only when it detects specific chemical cues from roots.

subsystems.name: Recognition elements
subsystems.role: bind to target molecules in root exudates, triggering shell degradation.

subsystems.name: Release mechanism
subsystems.role: converts the recognition event into a controlled release of nutrients.

subsystems.name: Soil delivery system
subsystems.role: carries capsules through soil to the root zone without premature release.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the nutrient core
buildSteps.detail: Dissolve or suspend nutrient salts and chelates in water or an organic solvent, then form nanoparticles 10–100 nm across by precipitation or emulsification.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the core
buildSteps.detail: Use emulsion polymerisation or nanoprecipitation to coat the nutrient particles with a thin polymer layer, controlling shell thickness to nanometre precision.

buildSteps.title: Add stimuli-responsive groups
buildSteps.detail: Graft pH- or enzyme-sensitive polymers onto the shell, or build the shell from monomers that include cleavable bonds that respond to root exudates.

buildSteps.title: Attach recognition elements
buildSteps.detail: Immobilise aptamers, imprinted polymer sites or enzymes on the shell surface so they bind specifically to organic acids, sugars or other root signals.

buildSteps.title: Test release in vitro
buildSteps.detail: Expose capsules to synthetic root-exudate solutions and measure nutrient release using spectrophotometry or chromatography to confirm signal-triggered behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Run greenhouse trials
buildSteps.detail: Apply capsules to potted plants in controlled conditions, track nutrient uptake and plant growth, and compare with conventional fertiliser.

buildSteps.title: Conduct field trials
buildSteps.detail: Test in real soil over a growing season, monitoring release, leaching, soil health and crop yield under varied moisture and temperature.

buildSteps.title: Scale up production
buildSteps.detail: Develop continuous flow reactors and quality-control methods to make uniform capsules in kilogram to tonne quantities.

buildSteps.title: Seek regulatory approval
buildSteps.detail: Assess ecotoxicity and fate of nanomaterials, then register the product under existing fertiliser or pesticide regulations.

prerequisites.why: nano-fertilisers exist commercially, but precise core–shell capsules with triggered release are still lab-scale.
researchers have identified many exudate compounds, but the exact signals that indicate nutrient demand vary by crop and environment.
pH- and enzyme-sensitive coatings are demonstrated in labs, but field stability and biodegradability need work.
nanoparticles often bind to soil particles or are filtered out before reaching roots, so delivery remains unreliable.
some countries have guidance, but global standards for nano-fertiliser safety and labelling are still developing.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of nutrient release triggered by pH or enzymes in simulated soil solutions
pathway.unlocks: proof that responsive nano-capsules can work in principle.

pathway.milestone: field trials of nano-fertilisers with simple triggers (pH, moisture) on staple crops
pathway.unlocks: data on yield gains, leaching reduction and soil behaviour.

pathway.milestone: integration of plant-specific signal recognition into shells
pathway.unlocks: fertiliser that releases only when a crop actually needs it, cutting waste.

pathway.milestone: commercial products tailored to major crops and soil types
pathway.unlocks: lower input costs and reduced nutrient runoff into waterways.
